Nyirkarasz Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nyírkarász, Hungary

Not demolished. Nyírkarász's Jewish population, recorded with 8 residents in the 1747 census, grew to 220 by 1880 before settling around 164-170 through the 1930s-40s; local Jews worked mostly as shopkeepers and traveling merchants, alongside craftsmen and a few landowners, supporting a Talmud Torah and cheder. Thirty men were conscripted for forced labor in 1941; by 1944 the Orthodox community numbered 125 before deportation via the Kisvárda Ghetto to Auschwitz's Lager-C that May. Twenty-one Jews remained in 1949, but none by the 1960s; the synagogue was demolished in 1953. This cemetery appears on an 1870 cadastral map, with tombstones through 1942.
